before: A named operation that can receive arguments and return a result.
after: A named piece of work that can receive inputs and send a result back.

before: C11 foundation
after: C17 core

before: Text directing formatted input or output; each conversion must match the corresponding argument.
after: Text with marks that tell printf how to display the supplied values. Each mark must match its value type.

before: C11 foundation
after: C17 core

before: A fixed sequence of char positions; a C string stored there needs space for its zero terminator.
after: A fixed group of char storage units. A string stored there also needs room for its ending zero.

before: C11 foundation
after: C17 core

before: A value identifying a location, or a null pointer value that identifies no object or function.
after: A value that can refer to a location in memory. A null pointer refers to no object or function.

before: C11 foundation
after: C17 core

before: A file included to provide declarations and other preprocessing information.
after: A file included by source files to provide shared declarations and preprocessing information.

before: C11 foundation
after: C17 core

before: For the relational and equality comparisons here, int 1 means true and int 0 means false.
after: A check of two values. These C comparisons give int 1 for true and int 0 for false.

before: C11 foundation
after: C17 core

before: Converting C source into an executable through compilation and linking.
after: Turning C source into a runnable program by compiling and linking its parts.

before: A printf instruction such as %d that specifies how to interpret a matching argument.
after: A format mark, such as %d, that tells printf the expected value type and how to display it.

before: A situation for which the C standard imposes no requirements on program behavior.
after: A situation where C no longer promises what the program will do.

before: An integer pattern used to select or change chosen bits.
after: A number whose set bits select the positions you want to check or change.

before: An inner declaration hiding an outer name within its scope.
after: An inner declaration using the same name and hiding an outer name within that inner scope.

before: Continuing from one switch label into following statements without leaving the switch.
after: Continuing from one switch case into the next statements without leaving the switch.

before: An operator giving storage size in C bytes; an array object size differs from a pointer size.
after: An operator that measures storage in C bytes. Measuring an array and measuring a pointer give different information.

before: A single-quoted C character constant; an ordinary one has type int.
after: A value written in single quotes. An ordinary character constant such as A has type int in C.

before: The zero character that marks the end of a C string.
after: The zero character that marks the end of a C string. It is not the printable digit 0.

before: Formatting into storage with an explicit capacity and checking truncation or error.
after: Writing formatted text within a stated capacity and checking whether it was cut off or failed.

before: Parsing text while checking whether digits were consumed, the full input matched and the value fit.
after: Reading a number from text while checking that digits were found, the whole input was accepted, and the value fits.

before: A declaration specifying a C function’s return and parameter types.
after: A declaration listing a function's input types and result type before its body is needed.

before: Using a valid pointer to designate the object it points to.
after: Follow a valid pointer to read or write the object it refers to.

before: Giving a function a copy of each supplied argument value, including pointer values.
after: Give a function a copy of each input value. A copied pointer can still reach the caller's original object.

before: Moving a pointer by array elements within one array.
after: Move a pointer by array items, staying within the same array or exactly one position past its end.

before: The period during execution for which storage for an object is reserved.
after: How long storage for an object remains available during a program.

before: An access path that does not permit modifying the pointed-to value.
after: A way to read a value that does not allow writing it through that access path.

before: A pointer parameter whose contract permits NULL to omit an output.
after: An output pointer that a function explicitly allows to be NULL when no stored output is wanted.

before: A named component accessed with . or through a pointer with ->.
after: A named value inside a struct, reached with a dot or through a pointer with an arrow.

before: An alternative name for an existing type, not a separate allocation.
after: A C declaration that gives an existing type another name. It does not create a stored object.

before: A type with named integer constants used here to describe explicit states.
after: A C type with named integer constants, used here to describe states.

before: A union plus a separately maintained tag identifying the stored alternative.
after: Shared storage for alternative member types, plus a separate tag saying which member was stored.

before: A standard allocation function returning uninitialized storage or NULL.
after: A function that asks for storage without setting its values. It returns NULL if allocation fails.

before: An array allocation function that initializes allocated storage bits to zero.
after: A function that allocates array storage and clears its bits. For int items, that gives zero values.

before: Resizing an allocation, preserving the old contents up to the smaller size on success.
after: Resize an allocation. On success, keep its old contents up to the smaller of the old and new sizes.

before: The responsibility to release a resource; in C this must be maintained by program design.
after: Responsibility for releasing a resource when its use ends. C code must manage this rule itself.

before: A check that prevents unsigned multiplication from wrapping before allocation.
after: A check that the requested byte count will fit before multiplying the number of items by their size.

before: The number of allocated element slots, distinct from the initialized logical length.
after: The number of available storage slots, which can be greater than the number of filled items.

before: An independently stored record connected to another through a pointer.
after: A separately stored item connected to another item through a pointer.

before: A function reporting ordering by a negative, zero, or positive result.
after: A function saying whether the left item comes first, is equal, or comes after, using a negative, zero, or positive result.

before: Preprocessor conditionals that avoid repeated processing of a header in one translation unit.
after: A preprocessing check that prevents a header section from being included twice in one source compilation.

before: A name designating an entity only within its translation unit.
after: A rule keeping a name local to one source file together with its included headers.

before: Token substitution performed by the preprocessor, not an ordinary function call.
after: Replacing a macro name and its inputs with code before compilation.

before: Including or excluding source text using preprocessing conditions.
after: Choosing which source text to include before the compiler builds the program.

before: Compile-time selection of an expression according to a controlling expression’s type.
after: Choosing an expression from its type during compilation.

before: Responsibility for checking acquisition and closing a FILE stream exactly once.
after: Responsibility for checking that a stream opened and closing it exactly once after use.

before: An int result indicating no next character, with stream indicators distinguishing end-of-file from error.
after: A special int result meaning no character was returned. Stream indicators distinguish normal end of input from an error.

before: The specified order of octets representing a multi-octet value.
after: The chosen order of bytes that together represent a larger value.

before: A library error indicator meaningful only according to the called operation’s documented contract.
after: An indicator used by some library functions to report errors. Read it using that function's documented rules.

before: A control-flow route that releases already-acquired resources before returning a status.
after: A route through the code that releases acquired resources before returning.

before: A repeatable check protecting previously expected behavior against later changes.
after: A repeatable check that catches a later edit breaking behavior that previously worked.

before: Runtime instrumentation that detects certain errors on exercised paths, without proving all paths safe.
after: A tool that adds checks while code runs. It can find certain mistakes on tested paths, but cannot prove all paths safe.

before: Compiled output for a translation unit that still may need other definitions at link time.
after: A compiled part of a program that may still need other parts linked to it.

before: The array of command-line string pointers supplied to hosted main, followed by a null pointer.
after: The list of command-line string pointers given to main, followed by a null pointer.

before: Waiting for a thread to terminate and establishing synchronization before later observation.
after: Waiting for a thread to finish before continuing, so its completed work can be read afterward.

before: A mutual-exclusion object coordinating access to shared state.
after: A lock that lets one thread at a time enter work protected by that same lock.

before: The default atomic ordering that includes one total order of sequentially consistent atomic operations.
after: An ordering rule in which the sequentially consistent atomic operations fit one shared order.

before: A qualifier affecting accesses, without providing thread synchronization or atomic read-modify-write.
after: A rule for accesses that matter outside ordinary code. It does not make competing thread updates safe.

before: A rule keeping the count of occupied entries within the allocated storage bound.
after: A rule keeping the number of filled items at or below the storage capacity.
